{"analysis":"The goal is delivering the agreed Taggable automatic 50% discount: after the same person completes a paid purchase at any one configured prerequisite tour, an eligible later checkout automatically receives its associated 50% code before payment, with existing checkout behavior preserved (goal, flow_and_capabilities). The current owner clarification makes atom selection the choosing machinery, not a separate goal. The baseline’s intake-only authorization is historical context for these records.

The existing face-recognition, search, checkout and payment flow provides the product foundation. Owner statements describe successful selfie search producing results that enable checkout and payment, and assign same-person establishment to the existing face-recognition flow (flow_and_capabilities, prior_options). This establishes an existing flow in the supplied account, but not verified live identity matching or its connection to automatic discount eligibility. Successful server-side matches and resolution of prior purchases through that flow remain unverified integration dependencies.

ProductDiscount is recorded as present in the inspected checkout. It models product_discount and exposes discount code, amount, type, tour, status, usage, unique-batch fields and a tour relation (flow_and_capabilities). These provide an existing representation of discount records and their constraints. Its presence does not establish that qualifying 50% codes are configured or that automatic selection or application is implemented.

The historical TourDiscountPrerequisites migration and reader provide directed relationships from a checkout tour to prerequisite tours. Their completion record reports installation and five passing frozen cases against installed source in isolated SQLite (current_position, prior_options). This is evidence of a previously implemented and tested relationship structure. The expected migration and service paths were absent from the inspected checkout, so present availability is unresolved; live MySQL behavior and checkout integration were outside the proof.

The historical PriorTourPurchaseEligibility service provides a bounded eligibility component for prior purchases at configured prerequisite tours, consistent with the settled rule that any one qualifying prerequisite purchase suffices. Its service and unit test were reported installed, with seven of seven cases and 324 assertions passing against controlled owner-derived SQLite fixtures (current_position, flow_and_capabilities, prior_options). That record explicitly excludes checkout wiring and live discount application. The expected service was absent from the inspected checkout.

SearchPaymentEvidence provides historical composition of search, order and payment evidence. Its review reports validation through actual product services, dependencies and Eloquent model files, with 12 cases and 18 inputs repeated after copying the byte-identical service into the product (prior_options, obstacle_observations). Expected nested results and rejections matched while dependency hashes and database snapshots remained unchanged (decision_uncertainty). This establishes a controlled internal-service result, not production payment verification or discount eligibility. The expected service path was absent from the inspected checkout.

RecognitionPurchaseEvidence provides historical resolution from mapped face-recognition/search evidence to prior search, order and payment identities, including rejection of invalid evidence before delegation (prior_options). A recorded example resolves mapped externalImageId evidence through history 11, order 101 and payment 501 with recorded-success status (decision_uncertainty). Controlled proofs and promoted-path repetition support that internal resolution behavior, not live same-person recognition or checkout behavior (current_position). Its expected service path was also absent from the inspected checkout.

The historical 50% discount selector provides deterministic selection of an applicable code or none, explicit exclusions, preservation of attributes and existing members, and unchanged state. Its review reports 19 cases across 25 input executions passing again; the five code-selecting cases passed real verification as the same record and the extracted payment usage guard (current_position, flow_and_capabilities, prior_options). These are reusable behavioral and test records for code selection and compatibility with existing verification. They do not establish full payment behavior or automatic checkout application. The inspected checkout lacked the named selector method.

The installed input-interview machinery and approved frozen ten-question template provide supporting context collection and handoff capability. Live acceptance demonstrated correction handling and export of each original question once; packaged verification replayed 51 recorded calls with zero new model calls, matching prompts, schemas and the accepted handoff (latest_contribution, prior_options). Their contribution is preserving usable delivery context. The installed replay proves its recorded path, not general future reliability or any discount implementation.

The build-only atom builder provides a separate execution capability for an owner-approved bounded atom, with implementation, experiments, promotion, validation and contribution review in its recorded scope (prior_options). Twelve local checks passed using the captured assignment and installed skill bytes in an isolated repository without the selection skill; the installed controller read the run and source and installed files matched byte-for-byte (current_position). This supports reported installed build capability within those checks, without demonstrating delivery of the complete Taggable feature. The selection design itself is recorded as proposed and unproven, so it is design material rather than established executable capability (prior_options).

Across the historical product components, the supplied proofs remain available as evidence in this snapshot; recoverable source and test files are not established as available now. The recorded inspection found expected paths absent and zero references to the named services and selector on the inspected branch and head (obstacle_observations). That does not establish deletion, absence from other branches or worktrees, or absence of differently named equivalents (prior_options). No supplied record demonstrates the complete automatic discount through real checkout, deployment or production data."}
